summary: A modular monolith on Google Cloud Run using Go (Gin) with Google Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL and a Next.js client. Chosen for a senior team of 5 with a $1500/month budget and 50,000 users in 12 months.

frontend.justification: Next.js targets web, covering project.platforms=[web]. It reuses the team's skills (team.languages=[go, typescript]).

alternatives.why_not: Ranked 0.1 points lower: weaker on time to market (rated 3 vs 5, which your priorities weight at 3/5).
Ranked 0.4 points lower: weaker on scalability (rated 4 vs 5, which your priorities weight at 5/5).

tradeoffs: Needs a Node runtime for SSR
Framework complexity and frequent major changes
what_would_change: If the target platforms change (today [web]), re-check coverage: Angular is the next option.
If SEO stopped being critical and the app became highly interactive, a SPA framework would become competitive.

backend.justification: The team already knows go (team.languages=[go, typescript]), which Go (Gin) uses. A team.experience=senior team of team.size=5 gets Go (Gin)'s typed, structured API model (operations burden 2 vs capacity 5). Go (Gin) handles websocket connections for requirements.realtime=true. It can meet the requirements.p95_latency_ms=100 ms p95 target on Google Cloud Run. It supports an MVP within timeline.mvp_weeks=12 weeks given its rating of 3/5 for time to market.

alternatives.why_not: Ranked 0.6 points lower: weaker on scalability (rated 4 vs 5, which your priorities weight at 5/5).
Ranked 1.4 points lower: weaker on scalability (rated 3 vs 5, which your priorities weight at 5/5).

what_would_change: If the team changed languages (today [go, typescript]), re-rank: NestJS is the next best fit.
If scale.users_12_months passed 20,000,000, Go (Gin) would need horizontal scaling and caching (cap = its comfortable range).

database.justification: Google Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL suits scale.workload=write_heavy traffic with scale.data_volume_gb_12_months=200 GB after 12 months. requirements.multi_tenant=true: row-level security / schema-per-tenant patterns isolate tenants. It is acceptable under compliance=[gdpr] (attestations: pci_dss, hipaa, soc2, iso27001, gdpr). Its comfortable range (20,000,000 users) covers scale.users_12_months=50000. requirements.payments=true: transactional integrity favours a relational engine.

alternatives.why_not: Ranked 0.2 points lower: weaker on scalability (rated 3 vs 4, which your priorities weight at 5/5).
Ranked 0.9 points lower: weaker on maintainability (rated 3 vs 4, which your priorities weight at 4/5).

what_would_change: If users exceeded 20,000,000, add read replicas or caching, or shard.
If requirements.offline_support became true, a store with device sync (Firestore or CouchDB) would gain priority.

hosting.justification: Google Cloud Run fits the monthly budget (budget.monthly_infra_usd=1500 USD): estimated $10-175/month at scale.users_12_months=50000. It is compatible with compliance=[gdpr]; the legal obligations remain with you. A p95 target of requirements.p95_latency_ms=100 ms is realistic here. It supports persistent websocket connections (requirements.realtime=true). scale.traffic_pattern=spiky load is absorbed by container scaling.

alternatives.why_not: Ranked 0.1 points lower: weaker on time to market (rated 3 vs 5, which your priorities weight at 3/5); costs more (about $70-525/mo vs $10-175).
Ranked 0.5 points lower: weaker on time to market (rated 4 vs 5, which your priorities weight at 3/5); costs more (about $25-300/mo vs $10-175).
Excluded by a hard constraint: no persistent websocket support (requirements.realtime=true).
Excluded by a hard constraint: no persistent websocket support (requirements.realtime=true).

what_would_change: If scale.users_12_months grew beyond about 50,000,000 (its comfortable cap), move to a container or serverless platform on a hyperscaler.
If the budget rose or operations capacity increased so that AWS ECS on Fargate was affordable and operable, it would be the next choice (it scored 0.1 lower today).

The upper bound assumes components are not all at their high estimates at once (60% of the summed spread). Excludes taxes, engineers' time, payment-gateway transaction fees and SMS/OTP fees.
